validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no problems, soft points or warnings; the points below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named in one line up front (how much y changes for each 1 along) and the rule is stated in words with Bitesize's quote [1] on exactly those words.

One fully worked example with numbers computed from the rule (A (1, 3), B (4, 9): 6 ÷ 3 = 2), and the same line slid to (2, 5) and (3, 7) so a run of 1 shows m itself, the rate-per-one reading the brief asks for (Stump, notes 6.1).
The picture shows the cause, not just the effect: signed run and rise arrows whose directions give the sign, and a readout with brackets round each coordinate, as the course brief decided.

Thirteen screens alternate SHOW and DO (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 show; 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 do) and end on two mixed puzzles (12, 13). Each lesson 1 misconception in the brief has a puzzle with its own slip: upside down (2, 12), the lost minus (6, 13), brackets (8, 13), mixed order (8), and level against vertical (10).
Ohm's law is used only as the units example the brief lists for lesson 1, with [4] and [5] on the words their quotes support; laws from readings are left for lesson 5.
Example readings (10 V at 2 A, 25 V at 5 A; the tank's 300 and 500 litres) are labelled as example values; nothing is invented.
fix: False absolute: 'The gradient is always a measure of how steep the line is' adds 'always' to Bitesize's quote [2], and a line straight up has no gradient at all. Drop 'always' and say why a bigger rise or fall for each 1 along is a steeper line.

Causal step skipped: 'A straight line climbs the same amount for each 1 along wherever you are on it' is asserted, not explained. Add the reason from what he can see: that is what keeps it straight, as a change in the climb per step would bend it.

Causal step skipped on the sign: the explanation says which way the arrows point but not why a negative rise over a positive run gives a negative m, and the same-order rule (start from either point, keep it first top and bottom) is on screen 7 and in practice but missing from explain, so the dossier loses it. Add: starting from B flips both signs, a negative over a negative is positive, so m is the same; mixing the order flips one sign only.

The common misconception is not shown failing in explain: the upside-down slip (x over y, ED561782 in the brief) is in practice only. Show it failing with numbers on the worked example: 3 ÷ 6 = 0.5 would mean half a step up for each 1 along, which the triangle shows is wrong.
Units sentence skips a step: '15 V ÷ 3 A = 5 Ω' jumps from a division of volts by amps straight to ohms. Write 5 V per A first, then the ohm.

ignores misses what the units screens would wrongly suggest: their squares stand for different amounts across and up, so how steep the line looks depends on the scales. Say the gradient is read from the scale values, not by counting squares, and add that check to practice.
whatAmILookingAt does not say what Why? does on a puzzle screen, so the builder must guess. Say it draws the triangle and fills in the readout for those two points.

Numbers are incomplete or mislabelled for the builder: step 7's 'Starting from B' entry has value −3 but a label about −2; step 9's 5 is labelled 'run 0'; the slips' values for steps 4, 6, 10 and 13 are missing, so the hints cannot show each slip failing. Fix the labels and list every slip.
Practice's common mistakes name each slip but not how to catch it. Add the check for each (a sketch for the sign, the order for mixed differences, 'which one is up the side' for upside down).
The recap leaves out 'taken in the same order', half of what makes the sum come out right.

round2.fixed: All ten points above are fixed in draft 2; the validator reports no problems, soft points or warnings.
checked: No false absolutes left: 'always' is gone from the steepness sentence; 'nothing can be divided by 0' and '0 divided by any run is 0' hold at every setting.

Every number in explain, practice and the screens is computed from the rule shown and rechecked: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 (and 0.5 upside down); 2 per 1 at (2, 5) and (3, 7); −6 ÷ 3 = −2 and 6 ÷ −3 = −2; 6 ÷ 3 = 2 with brackets; 15 V ÷ 3 A = 5 Ω; 200 ÷ 4 = 50 litres per minute; −6 ÷ 6 = −1; the worked example −12 ÷ 6 and 12 ÷ −6, both −2.

Footnotes sit on words their quotes support: [^1] difference in y over difference in x, [^2] a measure of how steep, [^3] vertical lines undefined, [^4] volts per ampere, [^5] the V-I plot's slope is the resistance.
